questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Sakshi told her sister that her child had been coughing a lot.
options_en: Sakshi said to her sister, "My child was coughing a lot."
Sakshi said to her sister, "My child coughed a lot."
Sakshi said to her sister, "My child will be coughing a lot."
Sakshi says to her sister, "My child has been coughing a lot."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were+V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

She said that she had been dancing the previous day. (Indirect Speech)

She said, "I was dancing yesterday" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
told... thatsaid to
hermy
had been coughingwas coughing

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

She had been chosen by me, for her very graceful style of dancing.
options_en: I had chosen for her very graceful style of dancing.
I had chosen herself for her very graceful style of dancing.
I had chosen she for her very graceful style of dancing.
I had chosen her for her very graceful style of dancing.
questions.solution_en:
Option D is the right answer. Option A is eliminated as it fails to specify who had been chosen, while the original sentence clearly does so. Option B is eliminated as it uses the reflexive pronoun 'herself', which should only be used when the speaker is talking about himself/herself, not the third person. Option C is eliminated as it is grammatically incorrect, the pronoun 'her' must be used here, as it forms the object of the verb (the person to whom the action is done) and not the subject 'she'.

Note:

Reflexive pronouns are words like myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves and themselves. They refer back to a person or thing. We often use reflexive pronouns when the subject and the object of a verb are the same.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The old philosopher would often sit by the river in a ________(pensive) mood, contemplating the mysteries of the universe.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence requires a synonym for "pensive," which means engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought.

a) reflective - means relating to or characterized by deep thought; thoughtful. This is the most accurate synonym for "pensive."

b) playful - means fond of games and amusement; light-hearted. This is an antonym of "pensive".

c) perturbed - means feeling anxiety or concern; unsettled. While deep thought can lead to anxiety, "perturbed" is not a synonym for "thoughtful".

d) passive - means accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance. This is unrelated to being in deep thought.

The complete sentence is: The old philosopher would often sit by the river in a reflective mood, contemplating the mysteries of the universe.

Hence, the most appropriate synonym is option (a).

Mohan asked,' Do you live in the hostel, Zoya?'

Mohan asked Zoya whether she lived in the hostel.
Mohan asked if Zoya lives in the hostel.
Mohan asked me whether Zoya lived in the hostel.
questions.solution_en:
The question is directed to Zoya, not to the reader ('me'), and neither is it a general question. Hence options (a) and (d) are eliminated.

The verb must be changed from simple present to simple past. ('live' to 'lived'), as the reported verb ('asked') is in past tense.

When the question doesn't start with a 'wh-' word, the reporting verb is followed by an 'if' or 'whether'.

Hence, the correct sentence in indirect speech is: Mohan asked Zoya whether she lived in the hostel.

Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Option d) means unexpectedly or without warning. This refers to the manner of occurrence, not the source of information.

Complete sentence: I don't know all the details yet; I've only heard it through the grapevine. I need more concrete information.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation.

Alex diligently completed his homework assignments each night and reviewed his notes regularly. Meanwhile, his classmates often procrastinated, leaving their homework until the last minute and cramming for exams. As the semester progressed, Alex's hard work paid off as he consistently achieved top grades. Which of the following best describes Alex's attitude?
options_en: A penny saved is a penny earned.
Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.
Bite off more than one can chew.
The early bird catches the worm.
questions.solution_en:
Alex consistently completed his homework and reviewed his notes regularly, showing a proactive and disciplined approach to his studies. He didn't wait until the last minute to do his work, unlike his classmates who procrastinated. As a result, Alex consistently achieved top grades, demonstrating that his early and consistent efforts paid off. This aligns with the idiom "The early bird catches the worm," which means that those who act promptly or start early are more likely to succeed or gain an advantage. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

A penny saved is a penny earned: This means that saving money is just as valuable as earning money, emphasizing the importance of frugality and wise financial management.

Don't count your chickens before they are hatched: Advises against assuming success before it's certain or before all the necessary steps have been taken; warns against premature optimism.

Bite off more than one can chew: Refers to taking on more tasks or responsibilities than one can handle; attempting something that is too difficult or ambitious.

options_en: At the port, the van will have been arrived.
The port will be arrived by the van.
The port shall have been arriving by the van.

questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb [been] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Perfect. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Future Perfect.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)

For example:

She will have bought the gold. (Active Voice)

The gold will have been bought by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

An infinitive can act as:

I. A verb

II. An adverb

III. A noun
questions.solution_en:

 To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

Therefore, an infinitive can act as a noun as well as a verb.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Some parts of a sentence are jumbled up and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

Despite facing numerous challenges,

P. demonstrating that strength can emerge

Q. of life with resilience and optimism,

R. determination, navigating the complexities

S. she persevered with unwavering

even in the face of adversity.
questions.solution_en:
After reading all the parts thoroughly, we can say that S and R form a pair as S introduces the main idea of the sentence, setting the context by stating that there were numerous challenges and R follows, explaining how "she" faced these challenges with unwavering determination. Q comes next, providing details about how she navigated the complexities of life with resilience and optimism. P concludes the sentence, emphasizing the overall message that her actions demonstrated that strength can emerge even in the face of adversity. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.

(P) for maintaining ecological balance

(Q) and safeguarding numerous unique species

(O) protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial

(R) from extinction
questions.solution_en:
The sentence begins effectively with part (O) "Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial". The gerund phrase "Protecting biodiversity hotspots" acts as the subject, and "is crucial" is the predicate, establishing the main idea.

Part (P) "for maintaining ecological balance" is a prepositional phrase that explains why protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial, stating the first reason or purpose. So far: "Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial for maintaining ecological balance".

Part (Q) "and safeguarding numerous unique species" introduces a second, parallel reason, connected by the conjunction "and." It continues the explanation of the importance stated in (O).

Part (R) "from extinction" is a prepositional phrase that modifies "safeguarding numerous unique species," specifying what they are being safeguarded from. It completes the idea in (Q).

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is OPQR.

The sentence formed after rearrangement is: Protecting biodiversity hotspots is crucial for maintaining ecological balance and safeguarding numerous unique species from extinction.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
